analysis.title: Weekly Markets Monitor: Waller the Dollar (16 November 2026)
key_insights: LBMA Gold PM closed Friday 13 Nov at US$3,891/oz, down 3.9% w/w, the second-lowest level of the year and a 10.9% y-t-d loss. The drivers were a stronger-than-expected October US CPI and hawkish Fed comments, which lifted yields and the dollar.

Governor Waller raised the prospect of a 50bp Fed hike in December. Together with CPI of 0.4% m/m against 0.3% expected and elevated PPI, this raised expectations of a December rate hike. The report calls it the largest rate rise considered since 2022.

The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index (BBDXY) broke a cluster of technical resistance at 1,229/1,233. A sustained hold above it would suggest a large USD base has formed and the core trend has turned higher. Next resistance is 1,242, then 1,249 and 1,261. Support is 1,227, and the trend stays higher while above 1,217.

10-year TIPS yields are up about 30bp in November. 10-year real yields hold a large triangle continuation pattern, with resistance at the 2.975% y-t-d high, then 3.00% and 3.16%. The report calls the stronger USD plus higher yields a possible double whammy headwind for gold.

Gold is retesting key support at US$3,858/oz, the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement of the 2015-2026 rise. The market is also at a typical downside extreme, 10% below its 200-day average, so the report's bias is to look for a floor here. A sustained close below $3,858 exposes $3,820, then $3,605 (50% retracement) and $3,500, a 37% fall from the start-of-year peak.
Gold resistance is $4,000 first, then $4,147/$4,178 (November highs and 55-day average). The immediate trend stays lower while below those levels.

Gold positioning was mixed. Shanghai futures traders trimmed longs and near-term options positioning turned increasingly bearish. European and Asian ETF investors kept selling, while US ETF flows turned positive on Friday's equity sell-off and safe-haven demand.

Nvidia leadership turmoil dominated the week and drove volatility in global AI stocks. Nvidia earnings on Tuesday 17 Nov, with ongoing leadership discussions, could move broader AI sentiment, and any volatility could spill over into gold.
Other US data: housing weakened, with existing home sales down 5.5% m/m in October to a 3.75mn annual rate, a 16-year low. Jobless claims stayed low at 200k.

Ex-US data: UK Q3 GDP grew 0.7% q/q, raising expectations of further BoE tightening. Eurozone Q3 GDP was 1.3% y/y. China's October CPI eased to 0.7% y/y while PPI accelerated to 5.7%, and exports rose 35.2% y/y. India's October CPI rose to 6.09% y/y, above the RBI's 6% upper tolerance level.

Week ahead: Nvidia earnings (Tue), October FOMC minutes (Wed), an unprecedented Xi-Trump-Putin meeting in Shenzhen (Thu), US retail sales (Tue) and ECB speeches. The marginal gold impact of further Fed hawkishness is described as uncertain because more hikes are already priced in.
Major global equity indices ended the week higher while bond yields and the US dollar rose and oil eased. The S&P 500 closed at 7,561.7 (+2.51% w/w) and the Nasdaq at 25,136.3 (+2.27% w/w).
earnings_insights: Nvidia earnings are due Tuesday 17 Nov. The report gives no estimates and flags the print and ongoing leadership discussions as potentially important for broader AI sentiment and for gold via volatility spillover.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Hotter than expected. It raised bets on a December Fed hike and weighed on gold. Y/y rates were unavailable because October 2025 data is missing after last year's government shutdown.
Core also came in above the survey, adding to rate-hike expectations.
The fastest pace since November 2022. Producer inflation remains elevated, which supports hike expectations.
A 16-year low, showing weak housing against resilient labour markets.
The fastest quarterly pace since early 2024, raising expectations of further BoE tightening.
Growth edged higher on better industrial activity in Italy and lower unemployment in France.
Soft domestic demand. PPI accelerated to 5.7% from 5.0% on higher energy costs.
Above the RBI's 6% upper tolerance level, driven by food inflation. The trade deficit widened to US$39.9bn.
Headline sales could slow after September's boost from higher gasoline spending.
Expected flat, reflecting already accommodative borrowing conditions.

crypto_views: Bitcoin closed at 68,322, down 9.89% w/w and 22.05% y-t-d, against a y-t-d high of 97,922 and low of 58,055. The 9-week RSI is 31.37%.
risk_factors: A sustained close below US$3,858/oz would extend the gold downtrend toward $3,820, $3,605 and $3,500.
A sustained dollar hold above 1,233 on BBDXY, plus rising real and bond yields, is a double headwind for gold.
Nvidia earnings and leadership uncertainty could spill AI-sector volatility into other assets, including gold.
More hawkish Fed commentary or hot FOMC minutes could add to hike pricing, although the marginal impact on gold is unclear.
Persistent US inflation, with PPI at 6.5% y/y, adds pressure toward a December hike.
charts_described: BBDXY weekly: the text names a close above the 1229/1233 resistance zone, with next resistance at 1242, 1249 and 1261, support at 1227 and the trend higher while above 1217.
10-year US real yield monthly: the text describes a large triangle continuation pattern, with resistance at 2.975%, 3.00% and 3.16%, and support at 2.79% and 2.72%/2.68%.
Gold spot monthly: the text describes a rally capped well below the 55-day average and a retest of the 38.2% retracement of the 2015-2026 rise at $3,858/oz.
vol_and_positioning: Gold options positioning turned increasingly bearish in the near term, and Shanghai futures traders trimmed longs.

COMEX positioning chart: money manager net long 324t, other net long 209t, total net longs 533t, with COMEX gold at US$3,940/oz. COT data was delayed to Monday 16 Nov because of the Veterans Day holiday.
Gold ETF options 1M ATM implied vol: GLD 23.52 (+3.4 vs a month ago), IAU 22.69, SGOL 23.73. GLD 30-day realized vol is 25.98.
The report would be alert to a positioning washout if gold broke to $3,500.
Gold's 9-week RSI is 35.05% and silver's is 28.69%. The dollar's is 74.93%, near overbought.
geopolitical: Unprecedented Xi-Trump-Putin meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday, where current conflicts in various regions and trade relationships may be discussed.
Beijing extended its trade truce with the US by 2 months, to January 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Gold has held the $3,858/oz Fibonacci support and sits at a typical downside extreme, 10% below its 200-day average, so the report's bias is to look for a floor. US ETF flows turned positive on safe-haven demand after Friday's equity sell-off.
tension_points.bear_case: A stronger USD that broke BBDXY resistance, rising real and bond yields and Fed hike pricing form a double whammy headwind. Europe and Asia ETF holders kept selling, and Shanghai longs and options positioning turned bearish. A break would expose $3,820, $3,605 and $3,500.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained close below US$3,858/oz would invalidate the floor view.
